newsitem.title: USA: U.S West Coast crudes dip with WTI, Calif. surplus.
newsitem.headline: U.S West Coast crudes dip with WTI, Calif. surplus.

text.p: U.S. West Coast crudes were mixed Monday in early afternoon trade, with light grades lifted by stronger West Texas crude prices and heavy California crudes weighed by surplus stocks, traders said.
Turnarounds at plants operated by Mobil, Tosco, and Chevron left extra California crude in regional storage and forced companies to cut published prices late last week.
Traders said more crude flooded the market last week after a fire at Tosco's Avon plant cut the facility's intake.
"That was an unforeseen incident that put heavies down," a trader said.
Values for California heavy, or viscous, crude oils dropped 25 cents a barrel to range 50 to 25 cents under the posted averages of California oil companies.
Outright prices for Kern River, a representative heavy grade, were offered at $18.25 and bid about $18 Monday.
But Wilmington, a heavy grade produced in Long Beach, Calif., was sold in the range of 70 to 80 cents over posted averages, representing a rise from recent weeks amid natural production declines.
Light grades of West Coast oil rose as February spot trade rolled into higher-priced March barrels.
With no new ANS deals reported Monday and diffs flat at $1.45 under March WTI, outright prices were up 20 cents with WTI to $22.42/22.62 a barrel.
BP America, a key producer, was asking for $1.25 below March NYMEX, with bidders were as wide as $1.50 a barrel under.
